subject: Recap: security intake + on-prem "airlock" topology options
messages:
From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.inference.com>
To: Kara Voss <kara.voss@opticmed.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.inference.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.inference.com>
Date: Thu, 11 Jan 2028 15:22:00 +0000
Subject: Recap: security intake + on-prem "airlock" topology options

Hi Kara — thanks again for the call earlier. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we have a single reference for the team.

What I captured:
- Compliance posture: OpticMed is in the middle of a SOC 2 Type II readiness effort (control testing underway). You said a summary PDF and the questionnaire answers would be easiest for us to review.
- Regulations: GDPR applies for EU patients; HIPAA applies to US PHI. You flagged audit logging and data residency as must-haves.
- Deployment preference: On-prem / private VPC with a physically isolated "airlock" option for sensitive workloads (no outbound internet egress from model-serving subnet, limited management access).
- KMS/HSM: you require FIPS-compliant key storage and ability to bring-your-own-key (BYOK).
- Evidence & artifacts: network diagram, SOC artifacts, and vendor questionnaire to start.

Immediate asks from our side:
1) Please share any SOC 2 summary / interim report you can (high level).
2) A high-level network diagram (even a sketch) that shows where you want the inference cluster relative to your internal services and any downstream EHR systems.
3) Clarify whether outbound egress is to be fully blocked or allowed to specific update endpoints (e.g., package repo mirror).
4) Confirm whether you need HSM-backed signing and KMS integration timeline.

Attaching: redwood_vpc_airlock_options.pdf for reference (short primer on how we design "airlock" topologies and common egress controls).

Proposed internal owners / timeline:
- Jordan Blake: draft a sample deployment diagram and proposed subnet/nat/egr pattern by EOD 2028-01-12.
- Monica Patel: kickoff the vendor questionnaire intake and map gaps against SOC controls.
- Hannah (me): coordinate follow-up call and compile artifacts for your security team.

Next step: can we schedule a 30-min follow-up on Fri, Jan 13 to review Jordan's draft and go through the questionnaire? I propose 09:00 PST.

Best,
Hannah Schmitt
Sr. Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
hannah.schmitt@redwood.inference.com
+1 (415) 555-0126

Attachments: redwood_vpc_airlock_options.pdf (see section "egress options")

From: Kara Voss <kara.voss@opticmed.com>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.inference.com>
Cc: OpticMed Security <security@opticmed.com>, Andrew Liu <andrew.liu@opticmed.com>
Date: Thu, 11 Jan 2028 18:07:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Recap: security intake + on-prem "airlock" topology options

Thanks, Hannah — great summary. A few clarifications and I'm attaching two artifacts: a one-page SOC 2 interim summary and an internal requirements workbook.

Clarifications / answers:
- SOC 2: We do not yet have a Type II attestation but have completed control testing for the majority of security controls; the SOC 2 summary (attached) explains which control sets are in scope. Target for attestation: Q2 2028.
- Network diagram: we'll attach a very rough sketch later today; for now, high level requirements: the inference cluster must be in a dedicated VLAN/subnet with no default route to the internet. Management plane access should be via a jump host in a different VLAN with MFA and limited source IPs.
- Egress policy: we require "deny all" by default. Any allowed egress must be explicitly whitelisted and go through a vetted outbound proxy (we'd prefer no NAT into public internet).
- Keys: we require FIPS 140-2 validated KMS and plan to use our HSM for production keys. BYOK is a requirement for production workloads.

Attached: OpticMed_SOC2_Summary.pdf, opticmed_requirements.xlsx

Ask: Can Redwood produce a sample deployment diagram that shows both a fully air-gapped option (no egress, manual package sync) and a hybrid option (egress via approved proxy for updates)? We'd like to see how you handle model updates, patching, and telemetry blocking in both cases.

Happy to run the follow-up on Jan 13 at 09:00 PST — confirm?

Regards,
Kara Voss
Head of IT Security | OpticMed
kara.voss@opticmed.com
+1 (617) 555-4456

Attachments: OpticMed_SOC2_Summary.pdf, opticmed_requirements.xlsx

From: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.inference.com>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.inference.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.inference.com>
Date: Fri, 12 Jan 2028 09:11:00 +0000
Subject: Fwd: Recap: security intake + on-prem "airlock" topology options

Looping Jordan into this thread — Jordan, please own the diagram deliverable. Key ask: provide two diagram variants by EOD 2028-01-12 (today):
- Variant A: Fully air-gapped (no outbound network egress from model-serving nodes; manual sync process for model binaries; limited management via an isolated jump host).
- Variant B: Hardened private VPC with controlled egress through an outbound proxy/gateway and strict firewall rules; show where telemetry/logging (if any) is buffered and how audit logs are exported to OpticMed's SIEM.

Notes for the diagram: include subnet ranges (example-only), proposed ACLs, NAT/egress device choices, and KMS/HSM placement. If you identify trade-offs (cost vs operational burden), call them out briefly.

I'll start the vendor questionnaire and map high-risk gaps to our SOC control catalog. Hannah, please confirm whether we should propose a short SOC evidence checklist for OpticMed to prioritize.

Thanks — Monica
Security & Compliance Programs | Redwood Inference
monica.patel@redwood.inference.com
